title: Tamil Nadu: Where to Complain and Get Free Help
summary: Police complaints, free legal aid, Lok Adalat, consumer commissions and helplines in Tamil Nadu.
keyPoints: You can give a police complaint at any police station; for a serious offence it is recorded as an FIR, with a free copy to you.
Free legal aid is a right; if you cannot afford a lawyer, contact your District Legal Services Authority or call 15100.
A Lok Adalat award is final and binding, and no appeal lies against it.
For a consumer dispute, file online on e-Daakhil or call 1915.
Save the helplines: 112 for emergencies, 181 for women, 1098 for children and 1930 for cybercrime.

body.text: In Tamil Nadu there is a clear route for almost every problem. Here is where to complain and where to get free help.

items: You can give a complaint at any police station. For a serious (cognisable) offence, it is recorded as an FIR, and a free copy must be given to you.
If the offence happened elsewhere, the police still record a Zero FIR and send it to the right station.
Many districts also allow an online complaint on the Tamil Nadu Police citizen portal.
If the police refuse to register your FIR, go to the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate.

body.text: ⚖️ Free legal aid in Tamil Nadu

items: The Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority (TNLSA) and each District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) give free legal aid to those who qualify.
Free aid is available to women, children, members of SC and ST, disabled persons, victims of disaster or violence, industrial workmen, persons in custody and those below the income limit.
This includes free help from a lawyer, free court fees and free legal advice.
Helpline: 15100. You can also walk into your District Legal Services Authority office.
Lok Adalats settle disputes quickly and free of cost, with the help of a judge and lawyers.
An award passed by a Lok Adalat is final and binding, and no appeal lies against it.
They are often used for small money claims, motor-accident claims and family matters.
Tamil Nadu has a State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission and District Commissions.
File online on the e-Daakhil portal, or call the National Consumer Helpline 1915.
A District Commission handles claims up to Rs 50 lakh.
1930 - cybercrime and financial fraud. 1915 - consumer. 15100 - free legal aid.

body.text: Free legal aid is a right, not a favour. If you cannot afford a lawyer, ask for the District Legal Services Authority.

practicalSteps: For a police complaint, get the FIR number and a free copy.
For free legal help, contact your District Legal Services Authority or call 15100.
For a consumer dispute, try e-Daakhil or call 1915 before going to a commission.
exceptions: Free legal aid depends on the income limit and the category you fall under.
A Lok Adalat award cannot be appealed, so agree only when you accept the terms.

faqs.q: Is free legal aid really free?
faqs.a: Yes, for those who qualify by income and category. It covers a lawyer's help and court fees.

faqs.q: Can I complain to the police in another district?
faqs.a: Yes. You can give the complaint at any police station; they must record it and forward it.

misconceptions.myth: Legal aid is only for very poor people.
misconceptions.fact: It is available to many categories - women, children, SC/ST, disabled persons, workmen, persons in custody and those below the income limit.
